To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The glutamine amidotrasferase subunits from the anthranilate syntheases of Escherichia coli, Salmonella typhi murium and Serratiamarcescens are structurally homologous.
the glutamine amidtransferase (GAT), the first enzyme of tryptophane biosynthesis in bacteria, is a subunit of the anthranilatase synthetase (AAS), a complex of two nonidentical polypeptides.

(i) the GAT subunits of AS from E. coli, Salmonella ty-phimurium, and Serratia marecsens have similar molecular weights (approximately 20,000) and (ii) the GAT and PRT activities of the AS complex are associated with the same subunit of the complex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and function of the glutamine-amidotransferase subunit of the AS of E. coli (AS-GAT), S. typhumrium (STAS-GAT) and S. marcescen (SMAS-GAT).
the structure and properties of the glutamine amide transferase subunit of the AS-PRT complex from E. coli and of the small subunit of the anthranilates synthetase of Serratia maracescens.

the structural homology of the GAT and PRT subunits of the AS-PRT complexes from E. coli, Salmonella typhi-murium and S. marcesens and of the GAT, PRT and AS proteins from Pseudomonas aeruginosa, P. putida, A. calcoa-ceticus and B. subtili.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the large subunit of AS is structurally homologous to component I of E.coli and S. typhi-murium while the small GAT subunit is homologous to the GAT subunits of the AS-PRT complexes of E. coli,S. typhimurmurium, and A. aerogenses, and also to the GAT of AS of S. marcesscens,P. putida,B. subtilis and A. calcaac
the AS-PRT complex is composed of four subunits, two of which are identical and function as component I, while the other two are non-identical and function as component II.
AS of the enterobacteriaceae is composed of two subunits, one of which is a GAT, whereas AS of the pseudomonadaceae is a heterodimer of two non-identity subunits, one being the GAT.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GAT subunits of E. coli AS and of S. marcecescens AS are similar, and that of P. putida AS is different.
the GAT subunits of the ASs of E. coli4,21, S. typhi- murium10 and S. marcesens14, which have been sequenced, are all very similar in amino acid sequence.
AS of E. coli (AS-PRT), S. marcescen s (AS), S. typhirnurium and B. subtili s are structurally homologous and that the AS-PRT complex is derived from AS by the association of a GAT component.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the glutamine amidtransferase (GAT), which is part of the anthranilic acid synthetase (AAS), is a homolog of the GAT found in the tryptophan synthase complex (TS) of the same organism.
we have identified a new family of glutamine amidotrasnferases, which we term GAT-2.

the small subunit of the AS of S. maracescens, P. putida, B. subilus and A. caloaceticus is homologous to component II of the AS-PRT complex from E. coli and that this small subunit is the GAT component of the AS.
